answer: Because the copper index resolves every citation against the lagoon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the terrace audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 235 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 235 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 4480 identities would post 2478 proofs and burn roughly 9 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
